findings.claim: The claim-next slot upsert conflicts on (tenant_id, schedule_id, slot_on), so if the captured Manaus day (or the divergent UTC day) ever coincides with a seeded slot date for schedule 00000000-0000-7000-8000-000027000001 (seed/20-fixtures-rait.sql lines 183-184 seed slots on 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-15), DO UPDATE adopts the seeded row and keeps its id; CLAIM_ACTOR_SLOT/CLAIM_ACTOR_SLOT_UTC are then never created and the id-based cleanup in resetMutableState (lines 164-166) misses the touched row. Blast radius is contained: the update writes the same 'DISPONIVEL' value the seed already holds, the test still finds an available slot, and the next backend:test:prepare-legacy or upgrade-sensor rebuild drops and recreates the whole dedicated database, so no state escapes the tier.
findings.fix: In resetMutableState, additionally delete inf.rait_schedule_slot rows for schedule 00000000-0000-7000-8000-000027000001 by (schedule_id, slot_on) for OPERATION_DAY and UTC_OPERATION_DAY (or assert the upsert's RETURNING id equals the fixture id), so cleanup is keyed the same way as the insert conflict target.

findings.claim: today() resolves the availability day as the UTC ISO day (new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)) while the tenant timezone is America/Manaus; the fixture now guarantees a published DISPONIVEL slot on both candidate civil days (Manaus day always, UTC day when it differs), so the E2E passes for either day semantics and can no longer detect a future regression or deliberate change in which day the service uses for schedule/slot resolution. This is not a weakened gate for the contracted behavior — assertions are unchanged and both slots are legitimately published within the schedule's inclusive period_start..period_end window (line 1790) — but the tenant-civil-day question is masked rather than decided.
findings.fix: Track as product follow-up: add a directed unit or integration case that pins the intended day semantics (tenant-timezone civil day vs UTC day) for schedule/slot resolution, or change today() to derive the day in the tenant timezone; do not resolve it inside this fixture delta.

findings.claim: The repeated backend:test:prepare-legacy between the integration and E2E tiers performs a full DROP/CREATE via createDedicatedDatabase, which refuses when any client backend session remains on detran_r7_ctg1_a2; a pool connection leaked by the integration tier therefore fails this reset, and the driver's fallback restoreFreshPriorityV3Database (lines 39-50) applies the same zero-clients refusal, ending the run as an AggregateError with the mutated dedicated database left in place until the next run's prep. This is strictly fail-closed (no wrong-target or masked-failure path; the root error is preserved), so it is an availability hazard, not a correctness or safety defect.
findings.fix: Optionally, before the mid-sequence reset only, terminate lingering client backends on the dedicated database with pg_terminate_backend scoped to datname = 'detran_r7_ctg1_a2' and guarded by the existing DETRAN_PRIORITY_UPGRADE_BASELINE_RESET_AUTHORIZED flag; otherwise keep the current fail-closed behavior and rely on the next run's prep.

notes: Correctness of the remit fix verified: prepare-rait-priority-upgraded-legacy.mjs lines 106-113 run the closed SEED_PROFILE=legacy-upgrade profile after the historical baseline and the current apply.sh upgrade; the current seed/20-fixtures-rait.sql line 216 upserts draft 00000000-0000-7000-8000-000038000004 with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE including document_id = 00000000-0000-7000-8000-000012000010 (document seeded at line 47), which is exactly what the unchanged remit gate requires (rait-case-command.service.ts lines 1676-1686: status='assinada' AND document_id IS NOT NULL AND non-blank content_hash on the origin case). The prep proves it post-seed (lines 117-138: 20 legacy cases, legacy_unmapped_task0028 marker, signed_draft_document equality, priority tables present) and seed.sh lines 59-91 fail closed unless all 20 legacy cases pre-exist before the legacy-upgrade profile runs.

Sensor isolation verified: backend:test:upgrade (package.json line 39) runs the byte-pinned rait-priority-upgrade.integration.spec.ts whose beforeAll (line 670) re-runs prepareLegacyPriorityV1Baseline, which drops and rebuilds the dedicated database from the hash-pinned v1.1.0 fixture (assertFixtureBytes verifies every file against SHA256SUMS with an exact inventory match; sourceForSeed forces the historical 05-parameters.sql and 20-fixtures-rait.sql), so the current closed seed cannot enter the final directed upgrade sensor. The historical v1.1.0 seed still records drafts without document_id (line 216) — history is preserved, not rewritten — and its SHA-256 (8b20d084…) matches both the fixture SHA256SUMS pin (line 5) and this delta manifest, so the harness will accept it and no pin was silently regenerated.

Erase-before-E2E verified: run-backend-ci.mjs line 29 repeats backend:test:prepare-legacy after the integration tier; because that prep begins with a full DROP/CREATE of detran_r7_ctg1_a2 and replays baseline, upgrade, and closed seed, integration mutations (including inserted rows, not just updated columns) are genuinely erased before the E2E fixture assumes canonical state. The mandated order unit → prep → integration → prep → e2e → upgrade is intact and the final upgrade gate remains inescapable (single runner, exact filename filter with --passWithNoTests=false).

Claim-next time fix verified: the fixture captures one operation instant at module load and derives the America/Manaus civil day via Intl (lines 38-53); Manaus is fixed UTC-4 with no DST, so the UTC day is either equal to or exactly one day after the Manaus day, and the conditional second slot (lines 683-699) plus the decide-path pair of slots on OPERATION_DAY and OPERATION_DAY+1 (lines 628-640) cover both cases inside the schedule windows, which the service queries inclusively (period_start <= today() <= period_end, line 1790). Crossing local midnight mid-suite fails explicitly rather than silently changing availability, as the fixture comment states. Test assertions were not touched and resetMutableState deletes both claim and decide slot ids each reset.

Restoration on failure verified at three layers, unchanged or strengthened by this delta: prepare-rait-priority-upgraded-legacy.mjs lines 145-156 restore on any failure after the baseline (now including the new seed and proof steps) and rethrow the root error (AggregateError if restoration also fails); prepare-rait-priority-v1-baseline.mjs lines 398-409 restore on baseline failure after reset started; run-backend-ci.mjs lines 39-50 restore after any post-prep failure including the second prep, E2E, or a hard-killed upgrade run, preserving the root error. No failure path masks the original error and no path skips the upgrade gate.

Role separation and blast radius: the delta touches only fixture, prep, and driver bytes (Inspector/Engineer test infrastructure); the product service and the upgrade spec are byte-pinned in the manifests and their remit/decide/claim code paths contain no environment-conditional or fixture-conditional branches (no process.env usage in rait-case-command.service.ts). All destructive operations remain pinned to detran_r7_ctg1_a2 with owner, zero-client, and explicit authorization-flag checks; the ordinary seed profile is closed and validated by name before execution.

Limitations: read-only static review without shell or DB access — SHA-256 digests in the manifests were not recomputed, byte-identity of the 'unchanged' files (upgrade spec, product service, assertions) rests on the pinned digests plus inspection of the working-tree contents, and this verdict does not claim or substitute for a full GREEN runtime run, consistent with the prompt's framing that the prior 108/110 run's two failures are addressed by fixture/prep/driver changes only.
